question.text: Two parallel wires in the plane of the paper are distance <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math> apart. A point charge is moving with speed u between the wires in the same plane at a distance <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> from one of the wires. When the wires carry current of magnitude <math><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math>  in the same direction, the radius of curvature of the path of the point charge is <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> . In contrast, if the currents <math><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> in the two wires have directions opposite to each other, the radius of curvature of the path is <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> . If <math><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> , value of <math><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> is
